claim.pdf_says: SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1 / ASSIGN { TO { device-name-1 | literal-1 } ... [ USING data-name-1 ] | USING data-name-1 } / [ [ ORGANIZATION IS ] SEQUENTIAL ] .
claim.why_it_matters: The Format 4 diagram is scrambled: the brace around device-name-1/literal-1 is drawn spanning up into the SELECT line (cutting through '[ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1'), and the ellipsis that the PDF places after that brace (repeating TO's operand) is moved to the top of the brace above the SELECT line. Read literally, the markdown no longer says that device-name-1/literal-1 may be repeated after TO, and it splices the SELECT line into the TO choice. Formats 1-3 on pages 232-234 render the same ASSIGN clause correctly and can serve as the model.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 234 (printed 212) at 300 dpi. The printed Format 4 shows a clean 'SELECT [ OPTIONAL ] file-name-1' line, then ASSIGN with an outer brace over two alternatives: 'TO { device-name-1 / literal-1 } ... [ USING data-name-1 ]' and 'USING data-name-1', then '[ [ ORGANIZATION IS ] SEQUENTIAL ] .'. The ellipsis sits immediately right of the inner brace, on the TO line. The markdown page-234.md lines 46-51 draw the inner brace's top (╭ ╮ with the … ) above the SELECT line, run its │ bars through the SELECT line (splitting '[ OPTIONAL │ ] file-name-1 │'), and leave no ellipsis after the brace on the TO line. Read literally, the transcription drops the repetition of TO's operand and corrupts the SELECT line. Format 3 directly above on the same page renders the same ASSIGN correctly. A genuine normative notation defect, described accurately.
